6.A  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2024-018, a Resolution of the Planning Commission of the City
  of Palmdale approving Conditional Use Permit 23-0020 an application to establish a large
  Residential Care Facility located at 4036 Tournament Drive and find that the project is
  categorically exempt from environmental review.

Deputized Clerk Magallanes read the title of Resolution No. PC-2024-018.

Brenda Magaña, Planning Manager presented this item.
 Chair Henderson opened the public hearing.

Public testimony was heard from three residents in opposition to the item. The following concerns
were raised related to trash, medical waste, loud screams, barking dogs, and emergency vehicles.

Mr. Vikas Jindal, the applicant addressed the concerns as follows:

1. Trash and biohazard bins have been designated for medical waste disposal. We have ensured
  compliance with Los Angeles County and State Health Department’s regulations.
2. None of the residents have personal vehicles. Street parking is intended for public use.
3. Although emergency vehicles have arrived in some instances, these are not limited to this
  location. Calls may occur in any neighborhood.
4. As far as the barking dogs, none of the residents have any animals on the premises.
5. Screaming can be heard from any home in a neighborhood, not specific to our residential
  facility.
6. Our care facility is following all State regulations.

Commissioners and staff discussed the applicant’s understanding of the residents’ concerns and
confirmed that the Conditions of Approval would be adhered to. Staff informed the residents
opposing the permit that should future issues arise, Code Enforcement complaints can be
submitted online through the City of Palmdale website or the MyPalmdale app.

Brenda Magaña, Planning Manager noted that Vice Chair Elize has joined the dais and will not
vote on item 6.A.

Chair Henderson closed the public hearing.

Moved by: Commissioner Jones, seconded by Commissioner Olivarez

6.D  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2024-021, a Resolution of the Planning Commission of the City
  of Palmdale approving Conditional Use Permit 03-05 Major Modification No. 1, an
  application to construct a park and ride facility on approximately 15 acres at an existing
  Marie Kerr Park located at the northwest corner of Rancho Vista Boulevard and 25th Street
  West and adopt the Mitigated Negative Declaration and Mitigation Monitoring and
  Reporting Program prepared for the project.

Deputized Clerk Magallanes read the title of Resolution No. PC-2024-021.
 Brenda Magaña, Planning Manager presented this item.

Chair Henderson opened the public hearing.

Public testimony was heard from seven residents in opposition, and a petition containing 19
signatures was submitted for the public record. The various concerns related to the adverse
impact on the environment. Many of the residents in opposition fall under the Los Angeles County
jurisdiction.

Commissioners and staff engaged in discussions to address the following concerns:

  1. Public notices were sent to residents located within a 700-mile radius of the project site.
  2. Basins are intended to be used as a collection pit for stormwater and mosquito abatement.
  3. The pump station will be used to generate water for Citywide projects.
  4. The mitigation of dust control will comply with Antelope Valley Air Quality Management
  District regulations.
  5. Security will patrol, and cameras will be in place for surveillance of the improved facility.
  6. The parking facility will serve as overflow parking for events held at the Amphitheatre.
  7. Special events will be permitted and conditioned as required in a Minor Use Permit prior to
  commencing events that meet the required definition of commercial entertainment.
  8. The future use of a Drive-in theatre will display to the southwest of the site on a temporary
  projection screen and require the use of the car radio channel for sound.
  9. RV parking and generators will adhere to overnight stay rules and will be monitored by our
  City Code Enforcement office.
  10. Traffic improvements related to paving will have no significant traffic impact associated with
  park-and-ride facility.
  11. Property values will not be negatively impacted by these improvements.

Chair Henderson closed the public hearing.

Moved by: Commissioner Jones, seconded by Commissioner Olivarez

BACKGROUND

On July 13, 2022, City Council approved a Housing Agreement, through Resolution No.
HA 2022-002 to provide a City of Palmdale Housing Authority loan for the acquisition and
pre-development of the subject property, located along 30th Street East, approximately
1,000 feet south of Palmdale Boulevard.

Site Plan Review (SPR) 23-003 was approved by the Planning Commission on
November 9, 2023, through Resolution No. PC-2023-022, and Planned Development
23-001 was approved by the City Council on November 15, 2023, through Ordinance No.
1617.

SPR 23-003 approved the construction of seven residential buildings, one mixed-use
building, and associated outdoor recreation spaces in two phases located west of
30th Street East and approximately 1,000 feet south of Palmdale Boulevard. The seven
residential buildings will each include two, four-bedroom units with a connected studio
unit. The residential portion of the site also includes play areas for multiple age ranges,
picnic and outdoor gathering areas, and a garden. The mixed-use area will be located
along 30th Street East and will include six affordable studio units, 2,800 square feet of
office space, 4,200 square feet of community space, and outdoor gathering and picnic

Modifications

The applicant has requested modifications to the architectural design and site layout
which are necessary to meet project objectives and ensure the economic feasibility of the
project. The full list of modifications is provided in Attachments A and B. A summary of
requested modifications is provided below:

Community Center
   Replace the standing seam metal roof with a Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) standing
  seam design.
   Replace decorative metal panels with stucco.
   Replace the gabion wall with stone veneer.
   Convert the interior waiting area to the exterior courtyard.
   Increase studio private open space enclosure height to six feet.
   Move downspouts from the interior to the exterior of the building.

Townhomes
   Replace standing seam metal roof with PVC standing seam design.
   Replace the gabion wall with a burnished Concrete Masonry Unit (CMU) wall.
   Reduce typical unit size by 480 square feet to 3,084 square feet.
   Standardize roof plan for townhomes.
   Remove window sunshades from most elevations.
   Modify the doors and windows on the townhomes.

Site Design
   Replace swales with mounds to accommodate drainage requirements.
   Replace the steel shade structure with a grove of trees.
   Include sports courts within the Fire Department turnaround.
   Clarify Phase 2 scope. The project was approved in two phases, with a portion of
  the studio units in the community center and one townhome included in the
  second phase. The plans have been updated to more clearly reflect the phasing.
   Reduce the height of the fence and vehicle gate between residential and mixed-
  use area from six feet to three and a half feet.
   Relocate solar panels from roofs to carports.

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

The proposed project is Categorically Exempt from California Environmental Quality Act
(CEQA) review pursuant to Sections 15301, Existing Facilities and Section 15332, Class
32, of the CEQA Guidelines, which exempts minor changes to existing facilities.
Additionally, the proposed changes are minor in nature and do not significantly alter the
project as approved as an infill development. The project qualifies as in-fill development
because it consists of the construction of seven residential buildings, one mixed-use
building including residential, community, and office uses, and outdoor gathering spaces
on a site within the MU 1 (Mixed Use 1) zone, which allows the proposed uses. In addition,
the project occurs within the City, on a site of less than five acres, and is substantially
surrounded by urban uses with commercial development to the north, residential
development to the east, and a City park to the south. Furthermore, the vacant parcels
to the west of the subject site have been highly disturbed by vehicular and human activity.
